neighbours.label: Technology that enables a person to act: the 'to' or adverb after 'allows/lets/enables <person>' or 'capable of' when a device or system grants the ability, vs the same people choosing or wanting to act without an enabling technology
fire: The remote console allows the pilot to land the drone from a hundred miles away.
With the new app, customers are capable of automatically renewing their parking permits.
The software enables doctors to view scans from any hospital in the network.
A smart thermostat enables homeowners to adjust the heating while abroad.
The exoskeleton allows the patient to walk again after the injury.
Thanks to the plugin, writers are capable of instantly translating whole chapters.
Voice control enables drivers to send messages without touching the screen.
The new platform allows teachers to grade essays from their phones.
quiet: After a long discussion, the pilot decided to land the drone in the field.
Most customers wanted to renew their parking permits in person this year.
Several doctors hoped to view the scans before the meeting started.
Many homeowners refuse to adjust the heating until December.
After the injury, the patient promised to walk a little every day.
Some writers prefer to translate whole chapters by hand.
Most drivers try to send messages only when the car is parked.
Our teachers plan to grade the essays over the weekend.

predictions: Enabled-ability items reach 0.3-0.5; volition twins ('decided to', 'wanted to') stay under 0.1.
short: technology enabling a person to act
notes: Card: peaks on ' to' after 'allows the surgeon', ' automatically' after 'capable of', ' robot' in 'move between robot-based interaction'.
